**Solution 1 (257/78125): REJECT.** The complement reduction is fine, but the density formula is wrong. Summing $(\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i)^8$ over all independent sets $I$ of $C_5$ counts each 8-set once for every independent set containing its support, so singletons are overcounted inside the pairs. Inclusion-exclusion gives $5(2/5)^8 - 5(1/5)^8 = 255/78125$, not $257/78125$.

**Solution 2 (1/128): REJECT.** The two-disjoint-cliques construction does satisfy $\alpha(G)=2$, but it is not optimal. The $C_5$ construction below gives a strictly smaller density, $51/15625 \approx 0.00326 < 1/128 \approx 0.00781$. The claimed Zykov-symmetrization argument is also not valid as stated.

**Solution 3 (51/15625): ACCEPT.** Take $G$ as the blow-up of $C_5$ with five equal clique parts of size $m = n/5$, with complete joins between adjacent parts. Then $\alpha(G)=2$. An 8-clique has support in at most two adjacent parts, so the count is $5\binom{2m}{8} - 5\binom{m}{8}$. Dividing by $\binom{n}{8}$ and letting $n\to\infty$ gives $5(2/5)^8 - 5(1/5)^8 = 255/5^7 = 51/15625$. I did not re-derive the optimality of this construction; I am relying on the known extremal result for cliques in graphs with $\alpha \le 2$ (Lo's work on balanced $C_5$ blow-ups), which I recall but did not verify here.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
